episode.episode: Philips Hue: The smart home’s light bulb moment
episode.showDescription: Version History is a show about the best gadgets ever. And the worst ones. And the ones that might have changed the world, if they ever actually shipped. Every week, your favorite people from The Verge and beyond hang out to tell and debate the story of a gadget, app, website, or any other tech product, and try to determine the item’s true legacy. Because not every product is a hit, but every product has a story. And the ones that really matter aren’t always the ones you think. From the Verge and the Vox Media Podcast Network.
episode.episodeDescription: The humble light bulb might be the ultimate success story in the smart home. Our connected, adaptable homes are supposed to be customizable, connected to everything, and incredibly easy to use, and nothing has made that work quite like Philips Hue lights. In this episode, The Verge's David Pierce and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy are joined by smart home journalist and expert Richard Gunther to tell the Hue's story. We trace the product's history from its origins in the smartphone revolution, try to figure out how Philips managed to turn a staggeringly expensive lightbulb into a must-have gadget, and look at whether there's even more invention left in the future of lighting. We’re also on video! Check us out on YouTube. Subscribe to The Verge for unlimited access to theverge.com, subscriber-exclusive newsletters, and our ad-free podcast feed. We love hearing from you! transcript_window.text: It was very niche.

And for the most part, they were all one -offs.
You know, the thing that Philips did so brilliantly was opening it up.
Was making it compatible with everything.
They were promiscuously compatible with all of these different ecosystems that were also starting to come up at this time.
Because now as we started seeing a bunch of different smart products, now you had to figure out, well, how are we going to make them work together?
I don't have to have a separate app for every single one of them.

So you started seeing these systems that would either through software alone, like IFTTT or you know me, or through a big box of radios coming out with hubs like Wink and the first generation smart things.
These are all names I have not heard in so long.
This is so wild.
I mean, Staples Connect.
Oh, Staples was in this game.
And arguably, they had one of the best solutions out there.
Best yeah.
It was phenomenal.
Revolve, even Logitech Harmony at one point in time had compatibility with them.
They worked with Nest.
I mean, they worked with the expensive stuff, with Control 4 and Crestron.
They worked with everything, and they opened their API so third -party developers could build their own apps to control huge stuff.
It was brilliant.
And it's the exact opposite move that most companies would think as far as how to handle their IP.
And yeah, and actually that when I was asking George about the first, he said.
So I think we were the first internet connected smart light bulb, right, that was commercially available, right?
